newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B index rockets to year-high close.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B index rockets to year-high close.

text.p: Shenzhen's foreign currency B shares powered to a year-high close on Thursday, propelled by strong rises in the Shanghai B shares and general optimism about prospects for the market, analysts said.
The index gained 13.77 points or 8.57 percent to close at 174.56 as turnover burgeoning to HK$268.1 million from Wednesday's HK$89.4 million.
Brokers said the strong upward momentum was likely to extend into Friday.
Today's surge was led by Wafangdian Bearing Co in the morning but was quickly followed by other stocks.

All 44 B shares ended higher and a handful hit their 10 percent upper limits. "It seems the Shenzhen market is trying to catch up with Shanghai which has risen more than 20 percent this year," an analyst at J & A Securities said.

The Shanghai B share market ended Thursday at 82.392, up 5.522 points or 7.18 percent, scoring a year-high for the third successive session. At Wednesday's close, Shenzhen's B share index had only risen nine percent from the beginning of 1997.
"There is real zest in the market today with expectations of sentiment-boosting news soon," a trader at China Southern Securities said.

Today's surge was also linked to a report in the Shenzhen-based Securities Times last Thursday that Shenzhen was planning a series of measures to boost the B share market, an analyst at China Guotai Securities said.

The measures, previously reported, include the setting up of a new stock data network in Hong Kong and encouragement for more B share companies to obtain secondary listings on foreign stock exchanges.
"This shows the government is carefully nurturing the B share market," the Guotai trader said.
Analysts said strong performance by companies which had reported good 1996 earnings also boosted the index.
"Stocks like Wafangdian fuelled today's sharp rise," the Guotai analyst said.
Wafangdian rose HK$0.53 to its 10 percent limit-up of HK$5.83 on volume of 2.95 million shares.

Analysts said Wafangdian surged after the Shenzhen-based Securities Times on Thursday reported that its parent company, Wafangdian Bearing Group, would take over a high-technology company, Dalian Instrument Group.
A Wafangdian spokesman said the takeover would have no direct impact on the listed firm.
Shenzhen's A share index eased down 0.04 points or 0.01 percent to 461.31 on turnover of 8.49 billion yuan against Wednesday's 9.02 billion.
Shenzhen Development Bank was the most actively traded stock in the A share market, gaining 1.20 yuan to 29.10 yuan on volume of 43.8 million shares.
